page.layout: One column of index entries, numbered 2 to 26, with page references at the right of each entry. Above the column, the title "INDEX" in spaced capitals. Below the column, the catchword "LIBER" at the right.

main_text.head: I N D E X
main_text.l: 2 An possibile sit, ut corpus aliquod sine quantitate ad tempus existat? 464
3 An omne corpus per se sit finitum & circumscriptum; nullum vero infinitum & incircumscriptum? ibid.
4 An omne corpus per se in infinitum sit diuisibile? 465
5 An omne corpus sit in loco & quomodo? 466
6 An simpliciter impossibilis sit penetratio duorum corporum, sine alterius cessione? 467
7 An unum corpus possit simul esse in pluribus locis? 468
8 An duo corpora simul possint esse in uno loco sibi adaequato? 470
9 An corpus possit esse alicubi, sine certi spatii localis occupatione? ibid.
10 An omne corpus per se sit diuisibile in partes integrantes? 473
11 An omne corpus habeat figuram & quomodo? 474
12 An omne corpus per se sit sensile? ibid.
13 An possibile sit corpus per se sensile fieri insensile? 475
14 An continuitas & contiguitas sit propria corporum affectio? ibid.
15 An omne corpus per se habeat sex positionum differentias? 476
16 An corpus possit naturaliter transmutari in non corpus, aut ex non corpore fieri? ibid.
17 An corpus possit agere in spiritum, & vicissim spiritus a corpore pati? 477
18 An omne corpus sit materiatum? 478
19 An coelum supremum sit ens creatum? 479
20 An coelum supremum sit corpus & quidem immateriatum? 481
21 An coelum supremum in altissimo mundi loco supra alios omnes coelos naturales & aspectabiles sit collocatum? 482
22 An nec esse sit dari aliquam materiam primam? 483
23 An materia prima sit substantia? 484
24 An materia prima sit corpus, & quidem immateriatum? ibid.
25 An materia prima Deo fuerit coaeterna, an vero aliquando a Deo ex nihilo creata? 485
26 An sit discrimen inter corpus naturale & artificiale? 487

page.notes: The long s is printed as a letter resembling f in the scan; it is transcribed as s. Entries 2 to 26 are read as printed; the numbers at the start of each entry are as shown on the scan. The page number at the head or foot is not visible, so none is given. The Latin ligature for "&" is written as printed, and the abbreviation "&" is the XML-escaped form. No running head or signature is printed.
